paper_title: One-Electron Quantum Cyclotron as a Milli-eV Dark-Photon Detector
notes: Proof-of-principle measurement at 148.05 GHz (mA' = 0.612276 meV) setting epsilon < 3.2e-11 at 90% CL, ~75x better than previous constraints. Local DM density 0.3 GeV/cm^3. A projected future sensitivity (~8e-11 over 20-200 GHz) is also discussed but is a separate projection, not the measured limit. | Vision: Fig 5a. X-axis is mass offset from central m_A'=0.612276 meV (6.12276e-4 eV), spanning roughly ±1e-6 meV (full plot ±~1.2e-6 meV). U-shaped exclusion; minimum coupling epsilon < 3.2e-11 at center (from Eq. 8). Coupling type DarkPhoton (kinetic mixing chi/epsilon). XENON1T limit ~3e-9, Cosmology dashed ~3-4e-9. Mass conversions approximate since x-axis is a narrow band offset, not log scale. | CV calibration unavailable (no plot region), used LLM axes | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.03 snapped to identity)
